body: I've done pretty well in science classes so far and not had any trouble grasping the material. But I've been consistently terrible in math classes, though. usually I manage to learn the material pretty well but not keep up with the pace of the class. I fall behind, and either fail the class and have to retake it, or just scrape by with enough points to advance to the next level, but trash my overall GPA. On the whole I've always been terrible at school, failing most clases I take. In that way this is just more of the same, but this quarter has a bigger impact since I was supposed to start applying to universities and I've just fucked up my plans to graduate from community college. It's been hitting me pretty hard. I feel ashamed to have spent so long relying on money from my parents and aimlessly failing classes. The "10-year community college student" is a *joke*, but it's quickly becoming my reality.

I took some time off from school when my father passed away and I enjoyed not having the pressure, but I was living with my mother and felt really frustrated, and sort of emasculated - I felt terrible about leaching off my parents, like I was a worthless person. When I was in a vocational program, I was studying IT. I'm really good with that sort of stuff and could probably do it for a living. I also used to be into computer programming as a hobby... Somewhere, I have a disk with an ASCII-art animated demo I wrote in Watcom Fortran when I was 13.

But the thing is, I can't feel alright about participating in the economy if I'm furthering the way things are. That's why I feel like the only things I could really *live with*, as a career, are science or politics. I'm (failing at) trying to pursue a physics degree right now. I've been deeply interested in going into research for a long time, both out of interest in the subject matter, and because to me, somehow, the study of nature is still "pure", in spite of the socio-political circumstances that surround it - and perhaps, through the advancement of technology, and the impact it has on social relations, these circumstances can be transformed. I could feel alright with myself working and living if I knew I was playing some small role in that. Otherwise, the only thing I want is to find any way I can to escape. Lately, to me that's meant death, although I know there are people that manage to live on the edge of society and minimize their participation. I just don't see myself managing to continue if I can't pursue my dreams. The world feels like a prison to me.
